question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III AIF) holds an INR 1,000 par-value bond with an annual coupon of 14% maturing in 5 years. The required yield is 13%. Using PVA(13%,5)=3.517 and PV(13%,5)=0.543, what is the fair value of the bond?

explanation.text: The Logic: Value = 140 * PVA(13%,5) + 1000 * PV(13%,5) = 140 * 3.517 + 1000 * 0.543 = 492.38 + 543.00 = INR 1,035.38, rounded to INR 1,035.40. Since coupon (14%) > YTM (13%), the bond trades at a premium. Matches Example 12.2. The Trap: INR 1,000 ignores the premium; INR 1,023.50 uses an incorrect discount factor; INR 1,140 adds coupon undiscounted to face value without present-valuing. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/XIX-B fixed-income valuation uses identical PVA+PV formula. XV (Research Analyst) and X-B (IA L2) test bond math similarly.
